name: HeidelbergCement India Ltd
title: HeidelbergCement India Ltd - 500292 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Central India cement pricing under pressure from new capacity (JK, UltraTech ramp); management expects Q1 cost push of INR100-160/t to be passed on, but concedes near-term price weakness before monsoon ends; 95% utilisation and debottlenecked clinker give limited volume headroom.

summary.headline: HeidelbergCement India FY26 EBITDA rose 19.8% to a per-ton figure of INR584 (up 10%) as volumes grew 8.8%; company now debt-free.
summary.overview: FY26 showed higher EBITDA (up 19.8% YoY), PAT up 25.5%, and sales volume up 8.8%, with EBITDA per ton rising from INR530 to INR584. Q4 was weaker on price: gross realisation fell about INR105/ton QoQ, with INR53 raw material and INR25 other cost headwinds, only partly offset by power, fuel and freight. Management expects H1 FY27 cost pressure of INR100-160/ton (fuel and packaging), which it says it can pass on, though it expects prices to stay under pressure through the monsoon. The company repaid INR687 million of interest-free loans, is fully debt-free, and proposed a INR7 dividend per share.

segments.name: Cement (Central India)
segments.commentary: Clinker production about 3.05 million tons in FY26, running at roughly 90-95% utilisation of about 6 million tons grinding capacity. Clinker-to-cement ratio about 60-61%, targeted to fall 50-100 bps. Blended cement is about 97% of output.

segments.name: Premium and trade mix
segments.commentary: Premium products are 52% of trade volumes, up 9% YoY. Trade sales are 81% of total, with B2B at 19%.

segments.name: Logistics and fuel
segments.commentary: Road dispatches are about 45% of volume (up 1% YoY). AFR is about 11% (up 3% YoY). Lead distance is about 372 km. Petcoke share of fuel fell about 10 points to roughly 50-55%, with coal rising from 30% to 40%.

guidance_outlook: Industry demand in Central India expected to grow at least 7-7.5% in FY27; company volumes to track industry growth, constrained by near-full utilisation.
Q1 FY27 cost increase expected at INR100-150/ton (fuel mix, diesel, packaging); total H1 pressure INR100-160/ton, which management says can be passed on.
Prices expected under pressure through the monsoon (next quarter); firmer demand expected post-monsoon ahead of UP elections.
Capex about INR100 crore in FY27 and about INR120 crore in FY28, including sustaining capex of INR45-50 crore per year and the Khandwa blending unit (about INR130 crore over two years, backloaded).
Green power share targeted to rise above 40% in FY27-FY28, though management said a significant increase is unlikely.
Company has sufficient capacity headroom for the next 1-2 years.
capex_capacity: Khandwa (MP) blending unit: about 0.35 million tons (about 35,000 tons) of extra cement capacity; investment about INR130 crore over two years; CT received; completion expected within about 2 years.

Cement grinding capacity about 5.75 million tons (Central India) plus about 0.5 million tons at Karnataka, for total about 6.26 million tons as confirmed on the call. Clinker capacity about 3.1 million tons, with debottlenecking completed to about 3.23 million tons but awaiting government capacity approval.

Preferred bidder for two limestone mining leases in Madhya Pradesh: Kuria/Shivpur block (about 350 hectares, 62 million tons cement-grade limestone) and a second Shivpur block (about 105 million tons).
Gujarat plant: still awaiting government clearance; capacity figure of 2.5-4 million tons mentioned earlier, not finalised.
Karnataka: 3 million ton integrated plant under construction (not part of the listed entity).
demand_pricing: Central India pricing has been under pressure for several quarters due to new capacity (JK Cement, UltraTech ramp-up, other new cement operations).
Management expects Central India prices to follow Northern markets over the next year. It expects prices to stay soft until the monsoon ends.
Dalmia's integration of the JP assets, expected to add about 5 million tons from Q2, was raised by an analyst; management did not address it directly.
Clinker sales were said to be small and clinker was not purchased; sales volume figures were not split out.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 clinker production and what is the utilisation headroom and cement-to-clinker ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinker production was about 3.05 million tons in FY26, with cement capacity about 6 million tons and utilisation about 90-95%. Clinker ratio is about 60-61%, targeted to fall 50-100 bps; a new composite cement uses about 17% less clinker.

qa_highlights.question: What cost increase is expected next quarter and what levers exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a cost increase of INR100-150/ton next quarter. It sees INR100-160/ton as passable to customers. Fuel mix optimisation (petcoke to coal) could limit the impact to about INR150/ton versus the industry's about INR300.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Central India pricing weak, and can cost push be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new capacity (JK, a cement plant that came online, UltraTech ramp-up). It is confident of passing on cost increases with a lag but declined to forecast structural pricing beyond one year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the blending and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Khandwa blending unit adds about 0.35 million tons, costs about INR130 crore over two years, and is back-loaded. Total capex is about INR100 crore in FY27 and about INR120 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Clinker debottlenecking and capacity approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiln debottlenecking is complete, raising clinker capacity to about 3.23 million tons, but the government capacity approval is still pending. Grinding capacity is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for merger with Zuari and clinker sales volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a merger of group entities is planned eventually, but it would not set a timeline. Management declined to disclose clinker sales volume separately.

risks_watch: Central India price pressure from new capacity (JK, UltraTech, Dalmia/JP assets) may persist beyond the monsoon.
Fuel cost inflation from petcoke and diesel tied to the West Asia conflict; the company says it expects to pass on increases with a lag.
Macro risks: elevated headline inflation, currency depreciation (import-dependent), El Nino heat impact on rural demand.
Pending government approvals for clinker capacity (3.23 million tons) and the Gujarat plant.
Clinker ratio reduction and new composite cement ramp-up.
Fuel-cost disclosure (blended Kcal cost for Q4 and FY26) was not provided on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and cost pass-through, with cautious comments on near-term prices (under pressure through the monsoon). Evasive on several specifics: clinker volumes, blended Kcal cost, merger timeline, and Gujarat approval.
key_quotes: And as I've said before, I am confident, even though with a little bit of lag, the increase in input prices, we shall definitely be able to pass on to the customers.
So we do not see a problem with demand going forward.
Our impact may be around INR150 on account of this petcoke and diesel.

YoY; offset by gains on power and fuel, freight and other expenses

adds.what: Khandwa (MP) blending unit, about 0.35 million tons/yr extra cement capacity
Debottlenecking of clinker to about 3.23 million tons, awaiting government capacity approval

growth.why: Management guides Central India industry demand growth of at least 7-7.5% in FY27 with company volumes tracking it, but near-full utilisation (about 90-95%) caps volume; backing is partial via the Khandwa 0.35 Mt blending unit (~2 years away), debottlenecking awaiting approval, and claimed headroom for 1-2 years, while prices stay under pressure through the monsoon.
